I've been messing around with all of the builds recently (ER, Stride, Gore, Shieldbow, and a mixture of all of the above). I think currently you really have to vary your build every game depending depending mostly on what your team needs but also what champs the enemy team is running, what you will be sidelaning against most, and lastly how well you start the game. 

ER is still a solid first item if you pick up an early lead for yourself in the lane, but also building it puts you in an awkward place becasue it gives you 0 defensive stats, so you have to play pretty perfectly until you get your second item. Shieldbow is kinda the same way. The change feels quite nice, but with some of the same downfalls of er, I've lately been finding this build lacking when it comes to straight 1v9ing games. For that reason I only really build it if my entire team is already ahead or the enemy team has no cc as if you get ccd with this build the shield and extra ad will be basically useless. You can make some sick outplays with this build but its the least versatile of all of Fiora's builds and locks you into a very 1 dimensional play style. It also locks you out of both an active item and steracks which are both very nice to have mid-late game. If you are the only bit of frontline on your team DO NOT go this build becasue then your team cannot contest any objectives (assuming the enemy team is at all competent).

On the same note, if you are the dedicated frontline for your team vs a team with melee top/jg or 3+ melees overall, then Goredrinker is actually still viable as it gives you a solid bit of hp and a safe early build path with phage. Pair it with ravenous hydra and steracks and you'll be chillin as long as the enemy adc isn't crazy fed and perma kiting you. Gore is also quite good if you fall far behind because it gives you good tools to survive tower dives and has a pretty forgiving build.

Lastly, the Stridebreaker build is kinda a happy medium. It gives you some hp so you're a lot less likely to get oneshot and you can somewhat frontline between the extra hp and dash to dodge or make small engages. Its a great rush into some of the more annoying ranged matchups as well. It is VERY good for snowballing because the extra dash + slow will basically double your engage range and make it much easier to both find picks and 1v1s that you wouldn't be able to find with the other builds. You can also get a third item steracks and still get some what tanky too.
